forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Guildford forecasts £1.066m overspend for 2026-27, with Trade Waste Services underachieving by £0.487m and Environmental Services overspending by £0.350m on agency staff
news_drafts.lead: Guildford Borough Council is forecasting an overspend of £1.066 million against its revenue budget for 2026-27, with the shortfall driven by a sharp collapse in commercial waste income and rising temporary staffing costs. Trade Waste Services is underachieving by £0.487 million — 26 per cent of its budgeted income of £1.857 million — which the council has acknowledged reflects unrealistic original projections. Environmental Services is also spending an extra £0.350 million on agency and casual staff to cover vacant posts, with agency costs running above what permanent posts would cost. The council has delayed a Community Services staffing restructure that was meant to save money, adding a further £0.075 million to the overspend. A supplementary estimate of £200,000 for unbudgeted IT costs will be funded from reserves.

findings.paper_title: Item 12 (1) - Appointments to Surrey Pensions Authority - App 1 - Pensions Structural Changes Order
findings.headline: For 12 named exiting employers, including Guildford Borough Council, no exit payment or exit credit is due when fund assets and liabilities are split between East Surrey Council and West Surrey Council.
findings.detail: Regulation 64 of the Local Government Pension Scheme Regulations 2013 is amended so that, where the exiting employers are the named Surrey bodies, the fund's assets and liabilities are allocated between the two councils in proportions set by the Surrey Pensions Authority. The Authority must take actuarial advice and consult both councils before setting those proportions. No exit payment or exit credit applies in this case.
findings.matters: Exit payments and credits can be large sums in a pension fund split, so a waiver of them, and the method used to set the allocation proportions, is a specific term that finance officers at other councils facing a fund division would want to compare.
findings.figures: 12 named exiting employers, comprising Surrey County Council and 11 Surrey district and borough councils including Guildford Borough Council
findings.quote: no exit payment or exit credit is due under

findings.paper_title: Item 12 (1) - Appointments to Surrey Pensions Authority - App 1 - Pensions Structural Changes Order
findings.headline: The Surrey Pensions Authority may invoice East Surrey Council and West Surrey Council quarterly, and may require payment in advance of up to its own estimate of each demand.
findings.detail: Demands may be made quarterly for net expenditure in the periods of three months beginning 1st April, 1st July, 1st October and 1st January. The Authority may also require payment in advance on account, not exceeding its estimate of the demand, and not earlier than one month before the period begins.
findings.matters: Advance payment on account determines when cash leaves each successor council, which affects its cash-flow planning and the working capital it must hold for its share of pension running costs.
findings.figures: Quarterly periods of 3 months beginning 1st April, 1st July, 1st October and 1st January; advance payment not earlier than one month before the period commences
findings.quote: The Authority may require a payment in advance and on account of a demand

findings.paper_title: Item 12 (1) - Appointments to Surrey Pensions Authority - App 1 - Pensions Structural Changes Order
findings.headline: From 1st April 2027, the Surrey Pensions Authority's net expenditure is to be apportioned between East Surrey Council and West Surrey Council by population.
findings.detail: Article 5 requires the Authority's net expenditure in each financial year from 1st April 2027 to be split between the two successor councils in proportion to their populations. Net expenditure excludes costs and receipts that fall to the pension fund itself. Population is taken from Registrar General estimates certified as at 31st March 2027 and 31st March 2028, and every third anniversary after that.
findings.matters: A finance director at either successor council, or at another council planning a similar pension fund transfer, needs to know how the running costs of a shared pensions body will be charged and how often the shares are recalculated.
findings.figures: Net expenditure apportioned from 1st April 2027; populations certified as at 31st March 2027, 31st March 2028, and every third anniversary of 31st March 2028
findings.quote: must be apportioned between East Surrey Council(5) and West Surrey Council(6)

findings.paper_title: Item 12 - Appointment of members to Surrey Pensions Authority
findings.headline: The Surrey Pensions Authority will meet its own costs, and the paper says there will be no financial burden on West Surrey.
findings.detail: The Section 151 Officer commentary states that the new authority's costs will be met by the authority itself. Member allowances and administrative costs are to be met by the Authority following its establishment. The paper gives no £ figure for those costs.
findings.matters: Where a pension fund is separated from its former host council, the question of who bears its running costs is one a finance director at a neighbouring or reorganising council would want to see answered in writing.
findings.quote: The Surrey Pensions Authority will meet its own costs, and there will be no financial burden on West Surrey.

findings.paper_title: Item 12 - Appointment of members to Surrey Pensions Authority
findings.headline: The Surrey Pension Fund's administering authority changes to the Surrey Pensions Authority on 1 April 2027, when Surrey County Council is dissolved.
findings.detail: The paper says Surrey County Council is the current administering authority, and that local government reorganisation requires the fund to transition to a new administering authority from 1 April 2027. The Surrey Pensions Authority formally came into existence on 5 October 2026, and its first meeting must be held by 1 February 2027.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council going through reorganisation, or a lender to one, may want to track how a pension fund's administering authority is handed over and on what timetable.
findings.figures: 1 April 2027 (effective date); 5 October 2026 (formal existence); 1 February 2027 (first meeting deadline). No £ figures.
findings.quote: The effective date for the Surrey Pensions Authority becoming the Administering Authority for the Surrey Pension Fund is 1 April 2027
